body.content: If the Collatz conjecture is fundamentally about the 'mixing' of powers of 2 and 3, is there a version of the Baker's theorem on linear forms in logarithms that could bound the possibility of cycles? A cycle requires (3^k / 2^m) to be extremely close to 1. Maybe the covering principle is actually a gap in the distribution of {k log 3 / log 2}.
body.why_keep_this: Explores a quantitative analytic approach to the 'covering principle' involving transcendence theory.
